title: SDK progression playlist + smoke-tests & quickstart skeleton
content:
Purpose: This doc is a lightweight, opinionated plan for a developer-facing progression playlist that takes a new integrator from zero to a resilient sample app using the Redwood SDKs in ~60 minutes. The goal is a deterministic path that covers: authentication, simple text generation, structured output, streaming, retry/telemetry primitives, and a reproducible smoke-test suite. Why a playlist? - Developers are time-boxed: give a clear chain of small wins rather than a single monolithic quickstart. - Each step is a deliverable example + a one-paragraph explanation of the failure modes and when to escalate to support. - Playlist tracks map cleanly to telemetry probes and gating for product tours/interactive guides. Audience and scope: - Primary: software engineers (frontend/backends) integrating Redwood hosted API or Dedicated at prototyping stage. - Secondary: platform/infra engineers evaluating Private deployment mechanics (we include a single section on network configuration and env var patterns). - Scope: minimal working examples in JS and Python, plus a reproducible smoke-test harness that runs locally and in CI. No exhaustive API reference here. High-level progression (6 modules, ~10–15 min each) 1) Hello-Token: SDK auth and first call - Objective: get an authenticated call returning a small generated string. - Deliverable: tiny app printing model response and request latency. - Failure modes: invalid key, DNS/proxy, 401 vs 403 (explain). - Smoke check: CLI script that validates env var present and receives 200. 2) Shapes: structured output and schema enforcement - Objective: use function/tool calling or structured output template to return JSON with typed fields. - Deliverable: sample that validates output against a JSON schema and rejects/alerts on mismatch. - Failure modes: hallucinated fields, unexpected nulls, truncation. - Smoke check: sample validator run asserting schema pass/fail. 3) Stream & React: streaming responses and UI wiring (frontend sample) - Objective: connect stream chunks to incremental UI updates and handle mid-stream cancellations. - Deliverable: minimal React component demo (300 LOC) that streams a completion and shows a progress state. - Failure modes: partial payloads, connection drop, rehydration after reconnect. - Smoke check: automated headless test that asserts streamed tokens arrive in order and first chunk < 500ms. 4) State & Cache: KV caching and prefix reuse - Objective: show how to cache previous context/prefix and reuse KV cache effectively to reduce token costs. - Deliverable: server-side example using in-memory cache + Redis backing. - Failure modes: stale cache, cache poisoning, evictions. - Smoke check: performance test measuring token count reduction for repeated prompts. 5) Resilience: retries, timeouts, and graceful fallbacks - Objective: implement client-side retry with exponential backoff, circuit-breaker, and fallback to cheaper model variant. - Deliverable: retry helper library snippet plus config for fallback routes. - Failure modes: retry storms, duplicate side-effects, idempotency handling. - Smoke check: CI job that simulates transient 5xx and verifies fallback triggered and not more than 3 retries. 6) Ship & Verify: telemetry, smoke-tests, and local CI integration - Objective: wire up lightweight telemetry (request id, latency buckets, token counts) and add a CI smoke-stage. - Deliverable: sample GitHub Actions file and a smoke-test harness that runs the earlier checks as a single pipeline.
- Smoke check: end-to-end CI job exit code 0 on healthy responses, artifacts uploaded with request-level metrics. Minimal artifacts to produce per module (checklist) - 1 README (module overview, success criteria, quick commands) - 1 runnable sample (python/js) with <= 300 LOC - 3–5 assertions used by the smoke harness (exit non-0 on fail) - 1 paragraph on common errors + troubleshooting steps Telemetry & gating plan - Each example emits a probe (event) with keys: module, sample_id, result: pass|fail, latency_ms, token_estimate, user_agent. - Probes are configurable to PII-scrub mode for public samples. - CI gating: require module-level probe pass before marking module complete in the Playbook. Smoke-test harness (design) - Small Python CLI harness (pytest-based) that runs the checks in order and reports a consolidated JSON artifact. - Run modes: local-fast (skips streaming heavy tests), full-ci (runs all checks, longer timeouts). - Exit codes: 0 = all pass, 1 = non-blocking warnings, 2 = critical failure. Developer flows and scripts (examples) - Quick local: - export RW_API_KEY=... - cd samples/hello-token && ./run_local.sh - CI snippet (GitHub Actions): run smoke-harness with secrets.RW_API_KEY and artifact upload step. Acceptance criteria for GA-ready playlist - Each module has a green smoke check in CI for at least one official sample in JS and Python. - Average new-developer completion time <= 75 minutes (observed in 3 user tests). - Telemetry probes validated and no PII present in sample artifacts. - Docs: concise README + troubleshooting that resolves >80% of Slack triage questions (measured after pilot). UX/Docs writing notes - Keep READMEs intentionally short (3–5 steps). Link to deep-dive pages for advanced topics (quantization, Dedicated config). - Inline tips titled "When this fails" for each sample. - Use numbered progression and a small checklist inline at top so devs know the path. Open questions / decisions - Multi-language priority: which other languages beyond JS/Python matter for the pilot? (Go/Rust?) - Should the streaming demo use SDK streaming primitives or raw websockets for maximal clarity? - How aggressive should telemetry be by default for samples (sensitivity tradeoffs)? Next actions (next 2 weeks) - (Aisha) Draft module READMEs for modules 1–3 and push samples skeleton. - (Diego) Prototype smoke harness with exit code contract. - (Rina) Define telemetry probe schema and PII scrub rules. - Schedule 30-min playtest with two new hires to measure completion time. Notes to reviewers - This is intentionally prescriptive: the aim is to reduce decision friction for a newcomer. Point out any missing failure modes you want covered or additional CI constraints. Appendix: quick failures cheat-list - 401 on first call -> check key, warning content: "key invalid OR access not granted" - Streaming stops mid-way -> check network/proxy, increase keepalive, consider reconnect logic - Structured output validation fails -> add stricter prompt anchors or post-validate and re-prompt - High token usage -> enable prefix cache and review prompt length End.
